method: ig-viral outlier method on Indian tech creators. YouTube is the corpus: one paced yt-dlp --flat-playlist request per channel (last 40 Shorts; the last 30 long videos only when a channel had under 8 Shorts), 2.5 s apart, no parallel requests, no login, no vidIQ. Outlier multiple = views / that channel's own median for the same format; 3x+ is signal. Hook = the video title (hook_source 'title'), cleaned of trailing hashtags and channel-name suffixes. Captions were not pulled: single-video requests hit YouTube's 'confirm you're not a bot' wall after 19 videos, so per-video fetching stopped there and was not worked around. Those 19 give real dates and lengths; other dates are estimated from list position times the channel's dated cadence (marked 'est:'), or left null. 'Recent' = dated or estimated within 60 days, or among a channel's 15 newest Shorts when the title carries no older year. Instagram: no profiles were opened or listed. The 12 @rahulmhinduja reels come from the existing brain study (brain/creators/rahulmhinduja.md, 27 Oct 2026); one public reel URL was re-read with yt-dlp, and Instagram returned no view count. Formulas: a tech-title classifier (T1-T15, each mapped to the nearest ig-reel hooks.json id), because hooks.json's English spoken-hook patterns leave 77% of these titles unclassified. swipe.py was also run as-is on captured.tsv (all 3x+ rows plus per-channel controls) and wrote tech_swipe.md. Copy the formula, never the video; every row is attributed.

sample.date_range: Lists read 27 Oct 2026. The newest-first lists reach back about 6 weeks for daily posters and 2+ years for slow ones. Dated rows run from 2023-04 to 2026-10-22. Instagram reels: 6-27 Oct 2026. Recent window (60 days): 1486 videos, 148 at 3x+.

structure: Base rate: 14.3% of Shorts and 13.0% of long videos beat their channel median by 3x. In the recent window it is 10%: newer videos have had less time to collect views, so a recent 3x is worth more than an old one.

Practical test (28%), payoff tease (25%), head to head (21.5%), which-one question (19.7%) and first-person experiment (19.7%) are the only shapes clearly above the 14% base rate. Each of these promises a result the viewer can see.
First-person openers ('I sent', 'I went', 'I built', 'my') hit 3x 19.4% of the time vs 14.0% without (124 titles).
Titles with an ALL-CAPS word hit 11.1% vs 14.9% without. Shock words and emoji stacks have the lowest lift (0.83).
A current-cycle topic in the title (iPhone Duo/18, BBD, RAM prices, 25H2, RX 9060 XT) hits 16.6% vs 13.8% without.
Title length barely separates: median 9.0 words in the top third vs 8.0 in the bottom. 11+ word titles do 15% vs 13% for titles of 4 words or fewer.

Language does not move the multiple: Devanagari titles 13.7% vs 14.2%, Hinglish in Roman script 13.2% vs 14.3%. Regional channels (Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Marathi, Bengali) follow the same formulas.
A ₹ price in the title is 13.6% vs 14.3%. Everyone uses one, so it no longer stands out.
hookscore.py rates the top and bottom thirds the same (median 42). It scores English spoken hooks and cannot read titles, so ignore it for this set.

Series parts decay fast: PC Tech Talk's 'PC Build From Local Shop' went Part-1 0.95x, Part-2 81x, Part 3 3.8x, Part 4 1.3x. The hit came on part 2, so one flop doesn't kill a series, but the follow-ups ride the hit and then fade.
Length: 19 dated outliers had a median Short length of 60 s; Rahul's Instagram reels ran 42-179 s. The length evidence is thin.

works: Put the test in the title: boot time, battery drain, drop test, temperature, FPS. 24 of 85 practical-test videos beat 3x (28%) across 13 accounts. First-person field reports and experiments: Techbeast (18K subs, median 21K) did 'Will RAM Prices Go Down in 2027?' 37x, 'I Sent a Stranger to Buy a ₹1 Lakh Gaming PC' 26x and 'I Investigated RAM Prices in Nehru Place' 20x, all in the last ~6 weeks.

Price alarm while prices are rising: RAM/PC-price titles are the best formula in the 60-day window (5 of 23) and 27% for accounts under 100K.
Small accounts can win: 643 videos from accounts under 100K beat 3x 14.9% of the time, the same rate as the giants. The multiple does not depend on size.
doesnt: Shock words and emoji stacks (😱🔥🤯, INSANE, OMG): the lowest lift of any shape (0.83).
ALL-CAPS words in the title: 11.1% vs 14.9%.
Roast and expose titles: under-index in the top third and 1 outlier in 33 recent uses. Technical Dost and Gyan Therapy own this, and it is crowded.
Buyer warnings ('don't buy', 'mistake', 'before you buy'): 1 outlier in 34 recent uses. The format is worn out.
Sale-deal roundups (BBD, Great Indian Festival, Diwali): 180 recent videos, only 7.8% at 3x. Saturated.
AI-tool tips: 61 recent videos, 2 outliers (3%). GTA 6 hype: 14 recent, 0 outliers.
Plain product labels and numbered 'Top 5 under ₹X' lists in Shorts: both below baseline.
Vague 'secret / hack / trick' titles with no concrete action: they pull the one-trick formula below baseline even though specific commands work.
can_work: Test reels on his own rig (T13 + T10). He owns an RX 9060 XT 16GB, a Ryzen 5 9600X, 32GB DDR5-6000 and a 180 Hz Acer. 'FSR 4 on vs off', '1080p vs 1440p on a 9060 XT' and '30 minutes of Cyberpunk, here is the temperature' combine the two strongest formulas and need no review units. Reasoning: test titles hit 28% and head to head 21.5%, against a 14% base rate.

First-person experiments with office friends or Pune shops (T3), in the Techbeast shape: 'I gave my colleague ₹1 lakh to buy a gaming PC'. Reasoning: a channel with 18K subs got 20-37x on exactly this; it suits Srijan's unhinged-funny persona and his office-guy wrapper.

Specific one-command tips, symptom first (T6 done right): 'Your 180 Hz monitor is stuck at 60', or one PowerShell line. Reasoning: specific Windows tips hit 28.6% recently and 31% for small accounts, while vague 'secret' tips flop. This matches his 'one-tip reels' lane.

The buyer's question with his own answer (T9): 'RX 9060 XT 16GB or RTX 5060 Ti 8GB? I bought the 9060 XT, here's why'. Reasoning: 19.7% hit rate, and he has the receipt, which most question titles lack.

Price-alarm reels from his own receipt (T5): what his build cost then vs now. Reasoning: price alarm is the best formula in the last 60 days and the RAM crisis is still running; his real invoice is evidence nobody else has.

Funny PC-shop skits (T14/T15) as an occasional test, not a pillar. Reasoning: Gaming PC Wala shows comedy can hit 47-145x in the PC lane, but it is one account and joke titles are weak in the recent window. Run these as Trial Reels first.
Skip roasts, 'don't buy' warnings, sale roundups and AI-tool tips for now: all saturated in the recent window.
